sections.description: This section covers the patient's presenting symptoms, relevant obstetric history, physical examination findings, and initial laboratory workup. It emphasizes how clinicians systematically evaluated a pregnant patient with acute abdominal symptoms and established the initial clinical picture that prompted further investigation.
subtopics: Patient demographics and obstetric history (G1P0A1, BMI 33, advanced maternal age)
Presenting symptoms: acute abdominal pain and dyspnea at 21 weeks gestation
Physical examination findings: abdominal mass in left upper quadrant and pelvic mass on bimanual examination
Initial cardiopulmonary assessment and stabilization measures
Laboratory evaluation: complete blood count, inflammatory markers, and urine culture
Multidisciplinary team approach in evaluating pregnant patients with abdominal masses

sections.section_title: Diagnostic Imaging and Tumor Markers in Pregnancy
sections.description: This section explains the diagnostic modalities used to evaluate abdominal masses during pregnancy, including ultrasound characteristics, MRI findings without contrast, and the interpretation of tumor markers. It addresses the physiological changes in pregnancy that affect diagnostic test interpretation and the safety considerations for fetal protection.
subtopics: Ultrasound findings: cystic masses with vascularization and relationship to uterine structures
Non-contrast MRI: indications, safety considerations, and diagnostic value in pregnancy
MRI features of the masses: thick walls, inhomogeneous fluid content, and solid components
Tumor markers in pregnancy: CA-125 physiological changes and limitations of interpretation
Challenges in imaging interpretation due to gravid uterus and mass size ('steric bulk')
Role of serial CA-125 measurements in differential diagnosis and follow-up

sections.description: This section analyzes the differential diagnoses considered based on clinical and imaging findings, including decidualized endometriomas, cystic degenerating leiomyomas, and ovarian neoplasms. It explains the reasoning process leading to surgical intervention, balancing oncological concern, symptomatic deterioration, and pregnancy preservation.
subtopics: Differential diagnosis: endometrioma versus leiomyoma with cystic degeneration
Imaging features suggesting each diagnosis and diagnostic uncertainty
Risk stratification: oncological suspicion, risk of complications (torsion, rupture, infection)
Indications for surgical intervention during second trimester pregnancy
Impact of mass-related symptoms: restrictive dyspnea and intractable pain
Informed consent process and counseling for surgery during pregnancy

sections.description: This section describes the surgical approach, the unexpected intraoperative findings that changed the preoperative diagnosis, and the critical decision-making process. It covers the technical aspects of myomectomy during pregnancy, fetal monitoring strategies, and the rationale for conservative management of the remaining mass.
subtopics: Preoperative preparation and timing of surgery (21 weeks + 6 days)
Surgical approach: longitudinal xiphopubic laparotomy and its rationale
Intraoperative findings: pedunculated twisted leiomyoma versus preoperative diagnosis
Intraoperative decision-making: excision of upper mass, leaving caudal mass in situ
Fetal monitoring during surgery: documentation of fetal heart rate
Progesterone prophylaxis: mechanism, dosing, and role in preventing preterm labor
Antibiotic prophylaxis and treatment based on urine culture results

sections.section_title: Postoperative Care, Delivery Planning, and Outcomes
sections.description: This section covers postoperative management including anemia correction, obstetric follow-up, and the rationale for delivery mode. It explains how the presence of a residual pelvic myoma influenced delivery planning and discusses maternal and neonatal outcomes with postpartum follow-up.
subtopics: Postoperative complications: anemia management with iron supplementation and transfusion
Tocolytic continuation: hydroxyprogesterone caproate until delivery
Obstetric follow-up: fetal growth monitoring and surveillance schedule
Pathological findings: benign leiomyoma with ischemic necrosis from torsion
Delivery planning: indication for elective cesarean due to pelvic myoma obstruction
Timing of delivery: reaching term (37 weeks) to minimize scar rupture risk
Postpartum course: myoma regression and symptom resolution

sections.description: This section synthesizes the evidence regarding myomas during pregnancy, including epidemiology, pathophysiological changes across trimesters, and management guidelines. It highlights key clinical lessons from the case, including diagnostic pitfalls, conservative versus surgical management considerations, and the importance of individualized care.
subtopics: Epidemiology of uterine leiomyomas and adnexal masses during pregnancy
Pathophysiology: myoma growth patterns during pregnancy and postpartum regression
Diagnostic challenges: myoma mimicking adnexal masses on imaging
Conservative versus surgical management: evidence and indications
Myomectomy during pregnancy: risks, outcomes, and technical considerations
Mode of delivery considerations based on myoma characteristics
Key clinical pearls: multidisciplinary approach, imaging limitations, and avoiding overtreatment
